query: Help me understand what's worth attention in these goal records.

per_column.name: improvement_domain
per_column.rationale: Gives a clean grouping axis for what each goal targets. Values align well with the description text, though it largely mirrors the existing 'category' column, reducing incremental leverage.

per_column.name: primary_action_lever
per_column.rationale: Distinct, useful axis capturing the HOW of each goal, not present in original columns. Generally grounded (resource_optimization, process_improvement, marketing_sales all fit text), but row 2 maps after-sales support and personalized interactions to 'training_development', which is a stretch not clearly supported by the text.

per_column.name: target_metric_type
per_column.rationale: Useful for comparing how targets are expressed. However labelling is inconsistent: the cost-reduction 20% and meeting-time 20% decreases are 'percentage_increase' (mislabelled direction), which weakens grounding even if categorizable.

per_column.name: time_horizon
per_column.rationale: Strong analytical axis for prioritization by urgency. Samples (Q4->within_quarter, next fiscal year->within_year) read the text soundly, with NULL appropriately used when silent.

per_column.name: improvement_magnitude_band
per_column.rationale: Banding target sizes is genuinely useful for triage. But grounding is shaky: rows with explicit 78%->90% and 75%->85% (both ~12-15pt/absolute increases) are labelled 'absolute_target_only' while a 20% goal is 'standard_20pct', and the customer-sat 12-point jump is not really 'absolute only'.

per_column.name: scope_of_change
per_column.rationale: Good axis for assessing organizational reach/impact. Some inferences are warranted (across functions->company_wide) but others are unsupported specifics (customer satisfaction goal -> department_level is asserted where text is silent on scope).

per_column.name: has_baseline_value
per_column.rationale: Flags whether a from->to baseline is stated, useful for judging measurability/quality of goals. Sample values correctly track presence of explicit start figures (78%, 75%, 1000) vs absence.

per_column.name: metric_category_alignment
per_column.rationale: Detects mismatch between the goal's category and its assigned metric (e.g. Customer Satisfaction paired with Expense Ratio), a strong signal of data-quality issues worth attention. Samples correctly return False for clearly mismatched metric/category pairs.

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuinely new axes (action lever, time horizon, magnitude band, scope, baseline presence, metric/category alignment) that support triage of which goals are urgent, ambitious, well-defined, or data-flawed for the 'what's worth attention' query; only improvement_domain heavily overlaps existing 'category'. Grounding is mostly sound where evidence is available, but recurring issues drag it down: direction mislabelling in target_metric_type ('percentage_increase' for decreases), inconsistent magnitude banding, and scope inferences asserted where the text is silent.
